Definition: from G2596 and G2919; to judge against, i.e. sentence:--condemn, damn.
BiblicalUsage: To condemn is to pass the guilty sentence, and the men of Nineveh will rise and condemn this generation because they repented at Jonah's preaching, and the queen of the south will do the same. God condemned sin in the flesh by sending His own Son, and now Christ is at the right hand of God making intercession, so who is he that condemneth. The sentence has been passed, and it fell on Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the only condemnation that matters has already been carried out at the cross, and no other court can reopen the case. I hold that the risen Judge is also my intercessor, and that is why I am not afraid of the verdict.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
